conceptTour.title: Book One, concept by concept
conceptTour.label: Academy · Typed film
conceptTour.description: A typed film through the seventeen concepts of Digital Organism Theory, Book One, each with a picture and an analogy. It plays only when you press Play.

scenes.name: The struggle
scenes.title: “Work hard, play by the rules, and you will get ahead.”
scenes.note: Distress is individualized while the architecture producing it is preserved.
scenes.source: The American Millennial Manifesto · Chapter Two
scenes.description: A person stands at the centre while six cultural messages press in: Your worth is what you earn. Do not risk your place. If it pays, it must be progress. Protect what is yours. Everyone does it. You have no choice. Rings of pain pulse outward from the person.

scenes.name: The cultural trap
scenes.title: “How we do things” begins to feel identical to “how things are.”
scenes.note: The Western civilization many of us inherited is neither sacred nor identical to reality. It is a historical Painting.
scenes.source: Book One · Architecture of Continuity · The Painting
scenes.description: The view pulls back as a ring closes around the whole scene and locks: a cultural trap. Around the trap: time as money, attention as inventory, nature as raw material, human beings as units of production.

scenes.name: The setup
scenes.title: Frames turn continuity into curriculum.
scenes.note: Learning requires enough stability for actions to have legible consequences and enough freedom for more than one response to remain possible.
scenes.source: Book One · Architecture of Continuity · Reality Frames
scenes.description: The trap turns out to be one of several cultures inside a larger ruled frame, RF₀, marked stable rules, legible consequences, and more than one response.

scenes.name: The turn
scenes.title: Understand what shapes you.
scenes.description: The lock springs open, the trap opens, and the person rises out through the opening.

interludes.name: The human character
interludes.title: Ego defends the Character Little c has learned to call itself.
interludes.note: To protect its fears, Little c paints Ego around the body—and when Ego hardens into Arrogance, it blocks new experience from changing the Canvas.
interludes.description: On the Canvas, Little c sits in one corner inside a ring of fear. It paints Ego around itself in the shape of a body, which hardens as Arrogance stands at its edge and turns new strokes away.

closing.title: Become a student of your own experience.

trailer.title: Digital Organism Theory
trailer.subtitle: A pragmatic, testable framework for experience.
trailer.note: The opening of the film: nine shots, one idea each. Every line is a plain observation, a quoted view, or labelled as DOT’s proposal.

shots.label: Observation
shots.description: A single line draws a full-height human figure in the dark. It breathes once, and a heartbeat glows at its chest.
lines: Every observation begins as an experience.

shots.label: Perception
shots.description: Five streams — sight, sound, smell, touch, and taste — pour in from the edges and build a glowing world around the figure.
lines: Your perception is formed from sensory data.
The sensory apparatus is not the whole story.

shots.label: DOT’s proposal
shots.description: The view pulls back: the figure is an avatar at the edge of a living sphere, Little c, whose inner loop turns. Intent travels out to the body and experience travels back.

shots.label: The prevailing view
shots.description: The sphere dims. A hard measuring grid snaps shut around the figure, and cause-and-effect arrows press in from outside. The prevailing view is quoted: “You’re nothing but a pack of neurons” — Francis Crick, 1994.

lines.text: “You’re nothing but a pack of neurons.”

lines: Yet experience itself stays outside the equations.

shots.label: Who fills the gap
shots.description: The view pulls far back to a lattice of boxed figures, each with a ring of stress. Strings tug each figure from the hand of another figure above, who is boxed too.
lines: We map the world in detail; ourselves, far less.
Others fill the gap: markets, platforms, ideologies.

shots.label: The body’s signal
shots.description: Each ring of stress pulses toward a small jade opening above its figure: a signal to change course. Suppressed, the openings close, the boxes thicken, and every figure across the lattice dims and shrinks as the costs compound.
lines: The body protests: stress, anxiety, burnout.
We treat the signal more than its source.
The costs compound: division, despair, conflict.
At root, this is a problem of knowledge.

shots.label: Attention
shots.description: Everything stops. In one figure a jade point lights at the chest: Little c, noticed. Its box dissolves.
lines: Test this against your own experience.

shots.label: The architecture
shots.description: The jade point becomes Little c₁ in DOT’s architecture. The view pulls back through RF₀ and Big C to the T × E field that Big C emerged within.

shots.label: Digital Organism Theory
shots.description: The architecture rises above the title: Digital Organism Theory. A pragmatic, testable framework for experience.
lines: A pragmatic, testable framework for experience.

screeningFilms.title: You, the Observer, Belong in the Inquiry
screeningFilms.summary: A personal introduction to Book One through familiar moments: a short message, learning a skill, and the marks experience leaves behind. Explore the Canvas, the Painting, Fear, Love, and the possibility of a different response. DOT’s larger claims about consciousness and physical reality remain hypotheses to test.

acts.title: Start with an ordinary moment
acts.summary: Begin with a familiar moment: a one-word reply can carry more than one meaning. The feeling is real; understanding it takes questions, comparison, and a willingness to revise.

acts.title: Explore the model
acts.summary: Explore DOT’s proposed architecture: Big C emerged within T × E: T is primordial continuity—Time; E is the raw information source. The model’s starting assumptions invite prediction, evidence, and correction.

acts.title: Notice what experience leaves behind
acts.summary: Learning a skill changes what you can do even after practice ends. Explore the Canvas as what carries change forward, and the Painting as the patterns through which you meet the next moment.

acts.title: Make room for a different response
acts.summary: Notice when an old defense shapes a new conversation. In DOT, Love names the condition in which Fear no longer governs you, making room for truth, care, boundaries, and a different response.
